confirmed_note: Confirmed 2026-08-01 by the app owner. The app has FIVE tasks; the sixth DTA task (04_dev) is a development-phase task, not used in the test or in production, and is deliberately absent from this map.
purpose: Maps the dta-server's INTEGER task_id (assessments.task_id) onto this package's string task ids. Hand-authored deployment config, NOT derived from the checkpoint.
WARNING: An integer task id must never reach the model directly: `model_task_id` in tasks.json is a row index into the learned task-embedding table, and a wrong-but-valid index returns a plausible score with no error. Unmapped integers raise UnknownTask by design -- keep it that way.

how_it_was_confirmed.1: app 'your friend borrows money' == 03_m: 'Sinun ystävällä ei ole paljon rahaa, ja hän pyytää sinulta 100 euroa. Mitä sinä vastaat hänelle?'
how_it_was_confirmed.2: app 'cannot come to work' == 03_n: 'Sinä et voi tulla tänään kurssille/töihin. Sinä lähetät ääniviestin opettajalle/pomolle ja kerrot, miksi sinä et voi tulla.'
how_it_was_confirmed.3: app 'describe what you do at home' == 04_h: 'Kerro, mitä kaikkea sinä teet normaalisti kotona.'
how_it_was_confirmed.4: app 'what language you use and where' == 04_i: 'Kerro, mitä kieliä sinä käytät ja missä.'
how_it_was_confirmed.5: app 'describe the shopping picture' == 04_test (dta-task5). The suffix is the tell: 04_test is the task used in the actual DTA test, 04_dev the development-phase version. THE PICTURE IS NOT A DISCRIMINATOR -- csv/task_prompts/task_id_remap.csv marks BOTH as picture tasks ('~1 min pic: shopping habits' for 04_test, '~1 min pic: shop + shopping questions' for 04_dev), and it is the same picture. 04_dev's prompt merely spells out 'Kerro kuvasta' in its text while 04_test's does not; the picture is shown in the UI regardless. An earlier draft of this file mapped 5 to 04_dev on exactly that mistaken reading.

training_support.note: Recordings per task in the le40 training pool. Task 5 (04_test) has the thinnest support of the five, so its task embedding is the least-informed; treat per-task comparisons involving it with more caution.
